## Failure and data integrity

The service releases browser attachments after successful prepare only. Failed parser/unsupported-file operations retain the attachment and selected Profile target. Retry dispatch and runtime retry preparation both use the same deterministic facade path. Typed errors appear as safe error messages; stacks are not shown. Tests assert `invalid_pdf_header`, `resume_import_unsupported_file`, `agent_attachment_lost` and `agent_attachment_session_mismatch`.

The production-parity fixture uses real Registry → raw AgentExecutor → CareerToolGateway → CareerToolGatewayExecutor → BrowserAgentToolService → WorkspaceRepository, without Kernel. Its canonical JSON chain explicitly reviews, confirms a new Profile, checks rich work/project fields and editor-compatible experience text, then reimports, reconciles with the existing Profile, confirms and reads back the same rich fields. No Profile write-contract change.

Normal text Host preparation and non-import `career_evidence` metadata remain on the Hermes path; the new regression asserts no import executor invocation. Existing Hermes runtime/integration tests also passed.

## Environment limits

Development Webpack PDF loading failed after the now-working facade boundary: `TypeError: Object.defineProperty called on non-object` in `__webpack_require__.r` while importing `pdfjs-dist/build/pdf.mjs`. Browser debugger evidence is in `.p47c1-pdf-debug.log`. Production Turbopack build passes the actual PDF selection tests. The frozen PDF parser was not modified to address this separate development bundler issue.

Hermes integration/eval scripts initially needed permission to create their fixed temporary build directory outside the workspace. Elevated runs completed successfully. The first build encountered temporary integration type paths; restoring baseline tsconfig removed that environmental interference and the subsequent production build passed.

No real provider variance, personal PDF content quality, or Electron packaged acceptance is claimed.
